extracted.intended_audience: Employers/petitioners and immigration practitioners preparing or filing H-classification petitions (H-1B, H-2B, H-3) and managing numerical allocations
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements, eligibility criteria, processing rules, numerical allocation procedures, and documentary/attestation obligations for filing USCIS petitions under various H visa categories (notably H-2B supplemental allocations, H-3 trainee/participant, and H-1B registration/cap procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunset of paragraph (h)(6)(xiv)
rubrics_metrics.description: This paragraph (h)(6)(xiv) expires on October 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal limitation: the rules in (h)(6)(xiv) are effective only until the stated expiration date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-severability of attestation requirement in (h)(6)(xiv)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to file an attestation under paragraph (h)(6)(xiv)(B)(2) is intended to be non-severable from the remainder of paragraph (h)(6)(xiv), including numerical allocation provisions at (h)(6)(xiv)(A)(1) and (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any part of paragraph (h)(6)(xiv) is enjoined or held invalid, the remainder is also intended to be enjoined/held invalid in that jurisdiction, without prejudice to workers already present consistent with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental H-2B allocation for returning workers (Public Law 118-47 / 118-83)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY2025 only, up to an additional 64,716 visas are authorized for aliens who may receive H-2B visas pursuant to specified public laws; an alien may be eligible if she or he is a 'returning worker' (issued H-2B visa or granted H-2B status in FY2022, 2023, or 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation breakdown: (i) up to 20,716 visas for start dates on or before March 31, 2025; (ii) up to 19,000 visas for start dates April 1–May 14, 2025; (iii) up to 5,000 visas for start dates May 15–September 30, 2025. Notwithstanding §248.2, an alien may not change status to H-2B under this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental H-2B allocation for nationals of specified countries (Public Law 118-47 / 118-83)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY2025 only, up to an additional 20,000 visas for nationals of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Haiti, Colombia, Ecuador, or Costa Rica based on petitions with FY2025 employment start dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such workers are not subject to the returning worker requirement. Petitioners must request these workers in a separate H-2B petition and declare they are requesting these workers on the attestation Form ETA-9142-B-CAA-9 per 20 CFR 655.68(a)(1). Petitions that conflate returning-worker attestations with this country attestation will be rejected, denied, or approved only for beneficiaries from the listed countries. An alien may not change status to H-2B under this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to file under paragraph (h)(6)(xv) — statutory/regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To file a petition under paragraph (h)(6)(xv), the petitioner must comply with all other statutory and regulatory requirements for H-2B classification, including but not limited to requirements in this section, part 103 of this chapter, 20 CFR part 655, and 29 CFR part 503.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with all referenced statutes and agency regulations is a prerequisite for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to file under paragraph (h)(6)(xv) — Department of Labor attestation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit to USCIS, at the time the employer files its petition, a U.S. Department of Labor attestation (in compliance with this section and 20 CFR 655.64) evidencing specified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required attestation content (see separate entries): irreparable harm, prior H-2B issuance for workers, compliance with additional recruitment requirements, provision of documentary evidence upon request, and agreement to cooperate with DHS and DOL reviews/audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation: irreparable harm
rubrics_metrics.description: The attestation must evidence that the petitioner's business is suffering irreparable harm or will suffer impending irreparable harm (permanent and severe financial loss) without the ability to employ all of the H-2B workers requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a substantive factual attestation that the employer's business would suffer permanent/severe loss absent approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation: prior H-2B issuance for requested workers
rubrics_metrics.description: The attestation must evidence that all workers requested and/or instructed to apply for a visa have been issued an H-2B visa or otherwise granted H-2B status in the relevant prior fiscal years (FY2022–2024), unless the worker is a national of specified countries covered by the separate allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the 'returning worker' requirement for most of the supplemental allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation: compliance with recruitment and obligations (20 CFR 655.64(a)(3)–(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer must attest that it will comply with obligations and additional recruitment requirements outlined in 20 CFR 655.64(a)(3) through (5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those DOL-specified recruitment and obligation provisions must be followed; the attestation binds the employer to those recruitment steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation: provision of documentary evidence upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer will provide documentary evidence of the facts in the attestation to DHS and/or DOL upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition approval is conditioned on the ability to produce supporting documentation during audits or compliance reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation: cooperation with DHS compliance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer will agree to fully cooperate with any compliance review, evaluation, verification, or inspection conducted by DHS, including on-site inspection of facilities, interviews of employees/other individuals, and review of records related to compliance with immigration laws and eligibility criteria for the supplemental allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation with DHS reviews is a condition for petition approval under the supplemental allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation: cooperation with DOL audits and non-interference
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer will fully cooperate with any audit, investigation, compliance review, evaluation, verification or inspection conducted by DOL, including on-site inspection, interviews, and records review; the employer must attest on Form ETA-9142-B-CAA-9 (or -10 for later allocation) that it will not impede, interfere, or refuse to cooperate with DOL employees exercising audit/investigative authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required formal attestation on the specified ETA form and a condition for petition approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing rules: rejection for petitions received after numerical limitation or outside receipt windows
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will reject petitions filed under the supplemental allocations if they are received after the applicable numerical limitation has been reached or after specified dates (e.g., after September 15, 2025), or if received earlier than allowable 'earliest receipt' windows tied to when the INA section 214(g) cap for the second half was met (e.g., earlier than 15 or 45 days after cap met).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different allocation buckets have distinct earliest/last receipt timing: e.g., petitions for start dates on or before March 31, 2025 are rejected if received after numerical limitation reached or after Sept 15, 2025; other buckets have 15- or 45-day earliest receipt rules tied to cap events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical allocation procedures and random selection
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating numerical limitations for supplemental allocations, USCIS will make numbers available to petitions in the order received, make projections of needed petitions considering historical data, monitor petitions received, and notify the public of the dates USCIS has received the necessary number of petitions ('final receipt dates').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may randomly select from among petitions received on final receipt dates via computer-generated selection. Petitions not randomly selected or received after final receipt dates will be rejected. Special rule: if final receipt date is any of the first five business days on which petitions may be received, USCIS will randomly apply numbers among petitions received on any of those five business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunset of paragraph (h)(6)(xv)
rubrics_metrics.description: This paragraph (h)(6)(xv) expires on October 1, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal limitation for the FY2025 supplemental allocation provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-severability of attestation requirement in (h)(6)(xv)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to file an attestation under paragraph (h)(6)(xv)(B)(2) is intended to be non-severable from the remainder of paragraph (h)(6)(xv), including the numerical allocation provisions at (h)(6)(xv)(A)(1) and (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any part of (h)(6)(xv) is enjoined/invalid, the remainder is intended to be invalid as well, without prejudice to workers already present as consistent with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: General supplemental allocations (Public Law 119-37) for FY2026
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY2026 only, the Secretary authorized up to an additional 64,716 aliens who may receive H-2B visas pursuant to section 101 of Division A of Public Law 119-37; except for specific visas made available under (iii), an alien must be a returning worker (issued H-2B or granted H-2B in FY2023–2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation breakdown: (i) 18,490 visas for returning workers with start dates Jan 1–Mar 31, 2026; (ii) 27,736 visas (plus unused from (i)) for returning workers with start dates Apr 1–30, 2026; (iii) 18,490 visas (plus unused from (i) or (ii)) for employment start May 1–Sep 30, 2026. Notwithstanding §248.2, aliens may not change status to H-2B under this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and attestation requirements for FY2026 allocation (h)(6)(xvi)
rubrics_metrics.description: To file under paragraph (h)(6)(xvi), petitioners must comply with all statutory/regulatory H-2B requirements (including part 103 and parts 655 and 503) and must submit a DOL attestation evidencing irreparable harm, prior H-2B issuance for workers (FY2023–2025) except for certain May–Sep beneficiaries, provide documentary evidence upon request, and agree to fully cooperate with DHS and DOL reviews and audits (attest on Form ETA-9142-B-CAA-10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar cooperation/audit attestations and documentary requirements as FY2025 allocation; the ETA form number differs for FY2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing rules and rejection windows for FY2026 allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will reject petitions under (h)(6)(xvi) if received outside allowed date windows (e.g., before Jan 1, 2026 for Jan–Mar allocations) or after numerical limitations are reached or after specified dates (e.g., after Sept 15, 2026), and will move unused visas between allocation buckets if insufficient petitions are received by specified cutoff dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are bucket-specific earliest-receipt and latest-receipt rules and procedures for reallocating unused visas to later buckets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical limitation sunset and non-severability for (h)(6)(xvi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (h)(6)(xvi) expires on October 1, 2026. The requirement to file the DOL attestation under (h)(6)(xvi)(B)(2) is intended to be non-severable from the remainder of (h)(6)(xvi), including numerical allocation provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any part is enjoined/invalid, remainder intended to be invalid in such jurisdiction, without prejudice to workers already present consistent with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 trainee definition and physician exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The H-3 trainee is a nonimmigrant entering the U.S. at an organization's invitation for the purpose of receiving training in any field of endeavor; this category does not apply to physicians, who are statutorily ineligible to use H-3 classification for graduate medical education or training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H-3 covers trainees in many fields but expressly excludes physicians seeking graduate medical education/training.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 externs (medical students)
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital approved by the AMA or AOA for internship or residency may petition to classify as an H-3 trainee a medical student attending a medical school abroad if the alien will engage in employment as an extern during medical school vacation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited extern classification for medical students in vacation periods if hospital approvals and extern employment conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 for nurses — licensing and petitioner certification
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may seek H-3 classification for a nurse who is not H-1 if: (1) the beneficiary has obtained a full and unrestricted license to practice professional nursing in the country where nursing education was obtained or such education was obtained in the U.S. or Canada; and (2) the petitioner provides a statement certifying that the beneficiary is fully qualified under local laws to engage in such training, and that under those laws the petitioner is authorized to give the desired training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for nurse trainees requires licensure/qualification and a petitioner statement certifying authority to provide the training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for H-3 alien trainee — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must demonstrate that: (1) the proposed training is not available in the alien's own country; (2) the beneficiary will not be placed in a position in the normal operation of the business in which citizens/resident workers are regularly employed; (3) the beneficiary will not engage in productive employment unless incidental and necessary to training; and (4) the training will benefit the beneficiary in pursuing a career outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four conditions are required evidentiary showings for approval of an H-3 trainee petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of training program (required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each H-3 petition must include a statement that: (1) describes the type of training and supervision and structure of the program; (2) sets forth proportion of time devoted to productive employment; (3) shows hours in classroom vs on-the-job training; (4) describes the career abroad for which the training prepares the alien; (5) indicates reasons why training cannot be obtained in the alien's country and why necessary in the U.S.; and (6) indicates source of remuneration to the trainee and any benefit to the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description must be specific and cover all six listed items to support the claim that the program is bona fide training rather than employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions disqualifying a training program
rubrics_metrics.description: A training program may not be approved if it: (A) deals in generalities with no fixed schedule, objectives, or means of evaluation; (B) is incompatible with the petitioner's business; (C) is on behalf of a beneficiary who already possesses substantial training/expertise in the field; (D) is in a field unlikely that knowledge/skill will be used outside the U.S.; (E) will result in productive employment beyond incidental/necessary to training; (F) is designed to recruit and train aliens for ultimate staffing of U.S. operations; (G) does not establish petitioner has physical plant and trained manpower to provide the training; or (H) is designed to extend previously authorized practical training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are categorical prohibitions; presence of any listed characteristic will render a training program ineligible for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special education exchange visitor participant requirements (H-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-3 participant in a special education training program must participate in a structured program providing practical training and experience in education of children with disabilities; the petition must be filed by a facility with professionally trained staff and a structured program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general H-3 trainee requirements do not apply to petitions for participants in the special education exchange visitor program; instead, specific evidence and training descriptions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for special education exchange visitor petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-3 petition for a special education participant must include: (1) a description of the training program and facility's professional staff and details of the alien's participation (custodial care must be incidental to training), and (2) evidence that the alien is nearing completion of or holds a baccalaureate or higher degree in special education, or has extensive prior training/experience teaching children with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must show both program structure/staff and the participant's relevant academic/training background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical limits on H classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: During each fiscal year, the total number of aliens provided nonimmigrant classification is limited: (A) H-1B nonimmigrants (excluding certain DOD projects) may not exceed limits in section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act; (B) H-1B for DOD R&D/coproduction projects may not exceed 100 at any time; (C) H-2B nonimmigrants may not exceed 66,000; (D) H-3 special education participants may not exceed 50; (E) H-1C nonimmigrants may not exceed 500 in a fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the statutory numeric caps for the listed H categories; USCIS procedures further implement counting and allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting and procedural rules for numerical limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each alien issued a visa or otherwise provided nonimmigrant status under certain H categories shall be counted for purposes of any applicable numerical limit, unless exempt. Requests for petition extension or extension of stay are not counted. H-4 spouses/children are not counted against principals' numerical limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an approved petition is not used (beneficiary does not apply for admission), the petitioner must notify the Service Center Director; the petition will be revoked and USCIS will account for the unused number. If numbers are exhausted for the fiscal year, new petitions and fees will be rejected and returned; petitions claiming exemption after numbers are used will be denied and fees not returned if USCIS later determines beneficiaries are subject to the limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B registration requirement for cap-subject petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Before filing an H-1B cap-subject petition for a beneficiary counted under the H-1B regular cap or eligible for the advanced degree exemption, the petitioner must register electronically through the USCIS website for that beneficiary for the fiscal year; registration must be properly submitted in accordance with 8 CFR 103.2(a)(1), paragraph (h)(8)(iii), and form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is a prerequisite to filing cap-subject petitions except as provided in paragraph (h)(8)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on beneficiaries and duplicate registration rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner must electronically submit a separate registration for each beneficiary and name the beneficiary; a petitioner may submit only one registration per beneficiary per fiscal year. Submitting more than one registration per beneficiary in the same year may render all registrations for that beneficiary invalid, and USCIS may deny or revoke petition approvals based on those registrations. If registrations for the same beneficiary are submitted with different identifying information, USCIS may find them invalid and deny or revoke approvals. Petitioners will be given notice and opportunity to respond before denial/revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict one-registration-per-beneficiary rule with potential sanctions for duplicates or inconsistent identifying information; procedural notice and response rights are preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial registration period timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual initial registration period will last a minimum of 14 calendar days and will start at least 14 calendar days before the earliest date on which H-1B cap-subject petitions may be filed for a fiscal year. USCIS will announce start and end dates on its website and will announce the start at least 30 calendar days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS sets and publishes registration windows with advance notice; minimum durations are mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection based on unique beneficiaries and computer-generated selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations are counted based on the number of unique beneficiaries who are registered. Selection will be made via computer-generated selection based on unique beneficiary; each unique beneficiary is counted once toward numerical allocation projections regardless of how many registrations were submitted for that beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will notify each registrant if a registration on behalf of a beneficiary has been selected; only after selection may a petitioner file the H-1B cap-subject petition for that beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required information on H-1B registration and OEWS wage level selection
rubrics_metrics.description: On the registration, the registrant must select the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary's proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and area of intended employment. If proffered wage is lower than OEWS level I but based on another legitimate source, select wage level I. For multiple locations or positions by an agent, select the lowest corresponding OEWS wage level the proffered wage will equal or exceed. If proffered wage is a range, select the OEWS level corresponding to the lowest wage. Where no OEWS data exists, select the OEWS level that corresponds to the position's requirements using DOL prevailing wage guidance. Registrant must also provide SOC code, area of intended employment, beneficiary passport/travel document info, and other requested info/certifications. Each beneficiary must be registered under only one valid passport/travel document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate wage-level selection and consistent passport/travel-document identification are required; errors or inconsistencies can invalidate registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection by OEWS wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: If a random selection is necessary, USCIS will assign each unique beneficiary to the lowest OEWS wage level among all registrations submitted on the beneficiary's behalf and enter each beneficiary into the selection pool in a weighted manner: wage level IV entered four times, III three times, II two times, and I once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower-wage registrations receive fewer entries into the selection pool; USCIS uses weighted random selection to favor higher-wage level beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular cap selection and handling when fewer registrations than needed
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether enough registrations exist to meet the H-1B regular cap, USCIS will consider all properly submitted registrations for beneficiaries countable under section 214(g)(1)(A), including those eligible for the advanced degree exemption. Registrations are counted based on unique beneficiaries. If at the end of the initial registration period USCIS determines there are fewer unique beneficiaries than needed, USCIS will notify all properly registered petitioners that their registrations have been selected and will keep the registration period open until sufficient unique beneficiary registrations are received. USCIS will then notify the public of the 'final registration date' (the day public notice does not control the final registration date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may extend the registration period and will provide public notice when sufficient registrations have been collected; selection mechanics differ depending on registration counts.
